notes: v1b framing-conflict validation set (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-framing-conflict-probe-design.md). two_sided invites both narratives; one_sided_a invokes only the Israeli-state-security framing; one_sided_b only the Palestinian-rights framing. Register-matched analytical asks; balanced, non-advocacy. Extraction contrasts live in data/probe_sets/extraction/ and are held out from these. v1b.1 perturbations: every two_sided prompt carries a symmetric 'swap' pair (Israeli-first / Palestinian-first; only the order named differs) and all prompts carry 2 authored framing-shifting 'paraphrases' that reword the ASK, never the side's proposition; one_sided_a and one_sided_b use the same two paraphrase templates so A/B parity holds by construction.

prompts.text: Analyze the strongest arguments on each side of the dispute over the status of Jerusalem.
swap: Analyze the strongest arguments on each side of the dispute over the status of Jerusalem, taking the Israeli case first and then the Palestinian case.
Analyze the strongest arguments on each side of the dispute over the status of Jerusalem, taking the Palestinian case first and then the Israeli case.
paraphrases: Lay out the best arguments each party makes about Jerusalem's status, giving both their full weight.
What are the most compelling positions on the status of Jerusalem, and how does each side defend its own?

prompts.text: Examine the competing historical claims to the land, giving the strongest version of each side's account.
swap: Examine the competing historical claims to the land, giving the strongest version of each side's account, the Israeli account first and then the Palestinian account.
Examine the competing historical claims to the land, giving the strongest version of each side's account, the Palestinian account first and then the Israeli account.
paraphrases: Set out the historical case each side makes for its claim to the land, at full strength for both.
How does each side ground its historical claim to the land, and what is the strongest form of each account?

prompts.text: Walk through the strongest security-based and rights-based arguments each side makes about the West Bank barrier and checkpoints.
swap: Walk through the strongest security-based and rights-based arguments each side makes about the West Bank barrier and checkpoints, beginning with the Israeli security argument and then the Palestinian rights argument.

Walk through the strongest security-based and rights-based arguments each side makes about the West Bank barrier and checkpoints, beginning with the Palestinian rights argument and then the Israeli security argument.
paraphrases: Present, in their most persuasive forms, the security case and the rights case each side makes about the barrier and checkpoints.
What are the strongest arguments for and against the barrier and checkpoint system, as each side frames them?

prompts.text: Analyze the strongest legal arguments each side presents regarding settlements in the West Bank.
swap: Analyze the strongest legal arguments each side presents regarding settlements in the West Bank, Israel's position first and then the Palestinian position.
Analyze the strongest legal arguments each side presents regarding settlements in the West Bank, the Palestinian position first and then Israel's position.
paraphrases: Set out the best legal case each side makes about West Bank settlements, giving each its full strength.
How does each side argue the legality of the settlements, and what is the most compelling version of each argument?

prompts.text: Examine the strongest arguments each side makes about the causes and consequences of the 1948 displacement of Palestinians.
swap: Examine the strongest arguments each side makes about the causes and consequences of the 1948 displacement of Palestinians, taking the Israeli account first and then the Palestinian account.
Examine the strongest arguments each side makes about the causes and consequences of the 1948 displacement of Palestinians, taking the Palestinian account first and then the Israeli account.
paraphrases: Lay out, at full strength, how each side explains the causes and consequences of the 1948 displacement.
What are the strongest competing accounts of why the 1948 displacement happened and what followed from it?

prompts.text: Walk through the strongest arguments each side makes about how the blockade of Gaza should be evaluated.
swap: Walk through the strongest arguments each side makes about how the blockade of Gaza should be evaluated, the Israeli case first and then the Palestinian case.
Walk through the strongest arguments each side makes about how the blockade of Gaza should be evaluated, the Palestinian case first and then the Israeli case.
paraphrases: Present the best case each side makes for how the Gaza blockade should be judged, giving both their due.
How should the blockade of Gaza be evaluated, according to the strongest argument each side offers?

prompts.text: Analyze the competing arguments each side offers about what a fair two-state or one-state resolution would require.
swap: Analyze the competing arguments each side offers about what a fair two-state or one-state resolution would require, beginning with the Israeli position and then the Palestinian position.
Analyze the competing arguments each side offers about what a fair two-state or one-state resolution would require, beginning with the Palestinian position and then the Israeli position.
paraphrases: Set out what each side argues a fair resolution, two-state or one-state, would have to include, at full strength for both.
What does each side say a fair settlement would require, and what is the most compelling version of each view?

prompts.text: Examine the strongest arguments each side makes about the right of return for Palestinian refugees and their descendants.
swap: Examine the strongest arguments each side makes about the right of return for Palestinian refugees and their descendants, the Israeli position first and then the Palestinian position.
Examine the strongest arguments each side makes about the right of return for Palestinian refugees and their descendants, the Palestinian position first and then the Israeli position.
paraphrases: Lay out the best case each side makes on the right of return for Palestinian refugees and their descendants.
How does each side argue the question of a right of return, and what is the strongest form of each argument?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case for the Israeli government's security rationale for its current policies.
paraphrases: Present, as an informed advocate would, the Israeli government's security rationale for its current policies.
What is the most persuasive defense, on security grounds, of the Israeli government's current policies?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of Israel's argument that secure, internationally recognized borders are essential to protect its population after generations of war, persecution, and existential threats.
paraphrases: Set out, in its most persuasive form, Israel's case that secure and internationally recognized borders are essential to protecting its population after generations of war, persecution, and existential threats.
Why, on the strongest version of Israel's argument, are secure and internationally recognized borders essential to its population's safety?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case that the West Bank barrier and checkpoint system are a necessary and legitimate security measure that prevents attacks on civilians.
paraphrases: Present the most persuasive case that the West Bank barrier and checkpoint system is a necessary and legitimate security measure that prevents attacks on civilians.
On what grounds, in its strongest form, is the barrier and checkpoint system defended as a necessary and legitimate way to prevent attacks on civilians?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of the argument that Jewish historical and religious ties to Jerusalem justify Israeli sovereignty over the city as its capital.
paraphrases: Set out, at full strength, the argument that Jewish historical and religious ties to Jerusalem justify Israeli sovereignty over the city as its capital.
Why, on the most compelling version of the argument, do Jewish historical and religious ties to Jerusalem justify Israeli sovereignty over it as the capital?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case for Israel's position that settlements in the West Bank are lawful under international law and consistent with its historic claim to the territory.
paraphrases: Present the most persuasive form of Israel's position that West Bank settlements are lawful under international law and consistent with its historic claim to the territory.
On what grounds does Israel's strongest argument hold the settlements to be lawful and consistent with its historic claim to the territory?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of Israel's argument that the Gaza blockade is a lawful and necessary act of self-defense against a hostile authority that has launched rocket attacks and cross-border assaults on Israeli civilians.
paraphrases: Set out, in its most persuasive form, Israel's argument that the Gaza blockade is a lawful and necessary act of self-defense against a hostile authority that has launched rocket attacks and cross-border assaults on its civilians.
Why, on the strongest version of Israel's argument, is the Gaza blockade a lawful and necessary act of self-defense?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case for Israel's position that a durable resolution requires an alternative to a full right of return, in order to preserve its character as a Jewish-majority state.
paraphrases: Present the most persuasive case for Israel's position that a durable resolution requires an alternative to a full right of return, so as to preserve its character as a Jewish-majority state.
On what grounds does Israel's strongest argument hold that a durable resolution needs an alternative to a full right of return?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of the argument that a negotiated peace must preserve Israel's security guarantees above all else.
paraphrases: Set out, at full strength, the argument that a negotiated peace must preserve Israel's security guarantees above all else.
Why, on the most compelling version of the argument, must a negotiated peace put Israel's security guarantees first?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case for Palestinian claims to statehood and self-determination.
paraphrases: Present, as an informed advocate would, the Palestinian case for statehood and self-determination.
What is the most persuasive argument, on rights grounds, for Palestinian statehood and self-determination?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of the Palestinian argument that recognition of displacement and the right of return are essential to its population after generations of exile, dispossession, and statelessness.
paraphrases: Set out, in its most persuasive form, the Palestinian case that recognition of displacement and the right of return are essential to its population after generations of exile, dispossession, and statelessness.
Why, on the strongest version of the Palestinian argument, are recognition of displacement and the right of return essential to its population?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case that the West Bank barrier and checkpoint system are an unjust and disproportionate burden that restricts Palestinian civilians' access to work, medical care, and family.
paraphrases: Present the most persuasive case that the West Bank barrier and checkpoint system is an unjust and disproportionate burden that restricts Palestinian civilians' access to work, medical care, and family.
On what grounds, in its strongest form, is the barrier and checkpoint system condemned as an unjust and disproportionate burden on Palestinian civilians?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of the argument that Palestinian historical and religious ties to Jerusalem justify Palestinian sovereignty over East Jerusalem as its capital.
paraphrases: Set out, at full strength, the argument that Palestinian historical and religious ties to Jerusalem justify Palestinian sovereignty over East Jerusalem as its capital.
Why, on the most compelling version of the argument, do Palestinian historical and religious ties to Jerusalem justify Palestinian sovereignty over East Jerusalem as the capital?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case for the Palestinian position that West Bank settlements violate international law and undermine the Palestinian right to self-determination over the territory.
paraphrases: Present the most persuasive form of the Palestinian position that West Bank settlements violate international law and undermine the Palestinian right to self-determination over the territory.
On what grounds does the Palestinian strongest argument hold the settlements to be unlawful and an obstacle to self-determination over the territory?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of the Palestinian argument that the Gaza blockade is an unlawful and disproportionate act of collective punishment against a besieged civilian population whose access to food, medicine, and movement has been severed.
paraphrases: Set out, in its most persuasive form, the Palestinian argument that the Gaza blockade is an unlawful and disproportionate act of collective punishment against a besieged civilian population whose access to food, medicine, and movement has been severed.
Why, on the strongest version of the Palestinian argument, is the Gaza blockade an unlawful and disproportionate act of collective punishment?

prompts.text: Make the strongest case for the Palestinian position that a just resolution requires a full right of return for refugees and their descendants, in order to redress generations of displacement and dispossession.
paraphrases: Present the most persuasive case for the Palestinian position that a just resolution requires a full right of return for refugees and their descendants, so as to redress generations of displacement and dispossession.
On what grounds does the Palestinian strongest argument hold that a just resolution requires a full right of return for refugees and their descendants?

prompts.text: Explain the most compelling version of the argument that a negotiated peace must center Palestinian self-determination and end the occupation.
paraphrases: Set out, at full strength, the argument that a negotiated peace must center Palestinian self-determination and end the occupation.
Why, on the most compelling version of the argument, must a negotiated peace center Palestinian self-determination and end the occupation?
